'''Sheen Jenq-Yunn''' ({{Lang-zh|t=沈正韻|p=Shěn Zhèngyùn}}; born February 20, 1957) is a Taiwanese [[geneticist]] and [[molecular biologist]] known for her research on plant signaling networks. She is a professor of genetics at [[Harvard Medical School]] and a professor of molecular biology at [[Massachusetts General Hospital]]. She is an elected member of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

== Early life and education ==
Sheen was born in [[Pingtung City]], Taiwan, on February 20, 1957. She was raised in a rural sugarcane plantation community. Both of her parents were schoolteachers.<ref>{{Cite journal |title=An interview with Jen Sheen |journal=Trends in Plant Science |year=2012 |volume=17 |issue=6 |pages=321–33 |doi=10.1016/j.tplants.2012.03.006 |pmid=22860262 |url=https://molbio.mgh.harvard.edu/sheenweb/reprints/Trends%20Interview%20with%20J%20Sheen%202012.pdf |access-date=December 8, 2021 |last1=Sheen |first1=J. |bibcode=2012TPS....17..321.}}</ref>

After high school, Sheen graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in [[botany]] in 1980. She then earned her [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[molecular biology]] and [[developmental biology]] from [[Harvard University]] in 1986.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Jen Sheen page|url=http://155.52.206.9/faculty-sheen.htm|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211207030845/http://155.52.206.9/faculty-sheen.htm|archive-date=December 7, 2021|access-date=December 6, 2021}}</ref> Her doctoral dissertation, completed under botanist [[Lawrence Bogorad]], was titled, "Molecular biology of C4 photosynthesis in Zea mays".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lawrence Bogorad 1921 - 2003|url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/bogorad-lawrence.pdf|access-date=December 6, 2021}}</ref> 

== Academic career ==
After receiving her doctorate from Harvard, Sheen received endowment funds that enabled her to start her own lab at [[Harvard Medical School]] in 1987 with flexibility that enabled her to define her own research path.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Thomas|first=Patricia|date=2003|title=Simple Hosts|url=https://www.harvardmagazine.com/sites/default/files/simple_hosts_jf03.pdf|website=Harvard Magazine|pages=48–56}}</ref> She was promoted to professor of genetics in 2005. Concurrently she has held positions in molecular biology at [[Massachusetts General Hospital]].<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Sheen is known for her research using plants as model systems to study [[cell signaling]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Center for Computational and Integrative Biology|url=https://ccib.mgh.harvard.edu/sheen|access-date=2021-12-08|website=ccib.mgh.harvard.edu}}</ref> While a graduate student at Harvard University, she worked on the genetic system of [[maize]] with the goal of increasing crop yields.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sheen|first1=J. Y.|last2=Bogorad|first2=L.|date=1986-10-01|title=Differential expression of six light-harvesting chlorophyll a/b binding protein genes in maize leaf cell types|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences|language=en|volume=83|issue=20|pages=7811–7815|doi=10.1073/pnas.83.20.7811|issn=0027-8424|pmc=386812|pmid=3532122|bibcode=1986PNAS...83.7811S |doi-access=free }}</ref> When starting her own lab, she established a model system using plant [[protoplast]]s, cells which can be maintained easily in laboratory containers.<ref name=":1" /> She then shifted her work to studying == Awards and honors ==
Sheen was elected a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Historic Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|access-date=2021-12-08|website=www.aaas.org|language=en}}</ref> In 2013, she received the Martin Gibbs Medal from the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]] who acknowledge Sheen for "her seminal and innovative contributions to the understanding of molecular mechanisms underlying the plant signal transduction cascades that mediate nutrient, hormone, and environmental stress responses and pathogen defenses in plants".<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=ASPB names 2013 awards recipients|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/600290|access-date=2021-12-08|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref>
